chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Shihab! Killing will increase among a household from Quraish to the extent that a man from among them will be called to the Caliphate, and he will refuse it.' Then he said: 'O Shihab! Do not say that I meant these sons of my uncle.' Shihab said: 'I testify that he indeed meant them.'
ai.seo_question: Which household from Quraish did Imam al-Sadiq refer to when predicting increased killing and a refusal of Caliphate?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) foretells a period of intense civil strife and martyrdom within the Banu Umayya, culminating in a caliphate offer that is ultimately rejected. The Imam’s instruction to Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih to avoid explicitly naming the family highlights the scholarly principle of *kitman* (concealment) to prevent premature political identification or sectarian conflict before the prophesied events unfold. This narrative underscores the transition of authority from the Umayyads to the Ahl al-Bayt, framing their rise as a divine resolution to the preceding turmoil.

en.hubeali: H 14901 – From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al-Hakam, from Hisham Bin Saalim, from Shahaab Bin Abdul Rabbahu who said:

Abu Abdullahasws said to me: ‘O Shahaab! There would be a great deal of killing in the households of Qureysh to the extent that the man from among them would be called to the Caliphate, he would refuse’. Then said: ‘O Shahaab! Do not announce that Iasws meant those sons of myasws uncle’. Shahaab said, ‘I testify that heasws was referring to them’.
en.sarwar: 454. Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al-Hassan Bin Muhammad Al-Kindy, from someone else, from Abaan Bin Usmaan, from Al-Fazel, from Zurara, who has narrated the following:

Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said that: ‘The people, when they did what they did, they pledged their allegiances to Abu Bakr, nothing prevented Amir-ul- Momineen (a.s.) calling the people to himself (a.s.) except that he (a.s.) looked around at the people and feared for them that they would renege from Al-Islam, and resort to worshipping the idols and not testify that there is no god except Allah (azwj) and that Muhamamd (saww) is the Rasool Allah (saww), and it was more beloved to him (a.s.) than he (a.s.) should agree with them upon what they had done rather than them reneging against the whole of Al-Islam. But rather, destroyed is the one who does what they did. So, as for the one who did not do that, and entered into what the people had entered into without knowledge or enmity against Amir-ul- Momineen (a.s.), so for that they have neither blasphemed nor exited from Al-Islam, and it is for that reason that Ali (a.s.) concealed his (a.s.) matter, and had to pledge allegiance unwillingly, when he (a.s.) did not find any helpers’.
